title: Week-to-week changes in training were not prospectively associated with injuries among Wisconsin high school cross-country runners
authors: Joachim MR, Heiderscheit BC, Kliethermes SA
population: Wisconsin high school cross-country runners (youth), daily surveys of distance, duration, intensity and RRI; 161 of 434 enrolled completed 75% or more of surveys
findings: 434 runners enrolled; 161 (37%) completed at least 75% of daily surveys and were analysed.

No associations between total weekly volume, total duration or week-to-week change in training characteristics (volume, duration, intensity, training stress) and in-season RRI in the following week (p>=0.54).
Sensitivity analyses at 50% and 90% survey completion found no significant associations.
Authors conclude RRIs are multifactorial and that interactions between training characteristics and other lifestyle factors likely need assessment.
limitations: Youth athletes, 37% analysed, self-reported daily surveys; the number of injury events is not in the abstract and power is unknown; null results do not show that progression is harmless. Not transferable to adults. The stored year is the online-first year (Crossref, 2024-07-31); the print issue is dated 2026 Mar (Injury Prevention 32(2)) in Europe PMC.
implications: Another null result for weekly change in a different population; it does not contradict treating the weekly ramp as a soft guideline and not a hard block. Consistency with Frandsen's weekly finding was not re-checked here.
Do not apply to adults or draw a youth rule from it; no age-specific rule is justified.
